chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the injuries in the fingers when the bone is exposed, [the compensation is] a tenth of the wergild of the finger, if the injured one does not intend to retaliate.
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a finger injury when the bone is exposed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmitting the judicial precedent of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS) regarding finger injuries, specifically establishing that exposing the bone triggers a fixed compensation of one-tenth of the finger's full wergild if qisas is waived. This ruling highlights the early development of Islamic jurisprudence in distinguishing between soft tissue damage and bone exposure, reflecting the precise quantitative methodology characteristic of the Ahl al-Bayt's legal teachings.
